fullPassage: To understand how breathing affects athletic performance, we first need to understand how the body makes energy from air and food. There are two options: with oxygen, a process known as aerobic respiration, and without it, which is called anaerobic respiration. Anaerobic energy is generated only with glucose (a simple sugar), and it’s quicker and easier for our bodies to access. It’s a kind of backup system and turbo boost when the body doesn’t have enough oxygen. But anaerobic energy is inefficient and can be toxic, creating too much lactic acid. The sickness, muscle weakness, and sweating you experience after you’ve pushed it too hard at the gym is the feeling of anaerobic overload. This process explains why the first few minutes of an intense workout is often so miserable. Our lungs and respiratory system haven’t caught up to supply the oxygen our bodies need, and so the body has to use anaerobic respiration. This also explains why, after we’re warmed up, exercise feels easier. The body has switched from anaerobic to aerobic respiration.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② generating → generated: 무산소 에너지는 몸에 의해 '만들어지는' 대상이므로 수동태 is generated가 맞다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① known: 'a process known as ~'는 '~라고 알려진 과정'으로, 과거분사가 앞의 명사(process)를 뒤에서 꾸며요. 맞아요.

❌ ② generating → generated: 에너지는 스스로 만드는 게 아니라 '만들어지는' 것이라 수동태(be동사+과거분사) is generated가 옳아요. 능동형 generating은 틀려요 ←정답

✅ ③ creating: 'can be toxic, creating ~'는 '~을 만들어 내면서'로 이어지는 분사구문이에요. 맞아요.

✅ ④ switched: 'The body has switched'는 현재완료(has+과거분사)로 '전환해 왔다'는 뜻. 맞아요.
det.tip: 수동태: 주어가 동작을 '당하면' be동사+과거분사 (is generated)

det.korean: ③ many → much: lactic acid(젖산)는 셀 수 없는 명사이므로 '많은'은 much를 써야 한다.
det.analysis:

questions.passage: To understand how breathing affects athletic performance, we first need to understand how the body makes energy from air and food. There are two options: with oxygen, a process known as aerobic respiration, and without it, which is called anaerobic respiration. Anaerobic energy is generated only with glucose (a simple sugar), and it’s quicker and easier for our bodies to access. It’s a kind of backup system and turbo boost when the body doesn’t have enough oxygen. But anaerobic energy is inefficient and can be toxic, creating too much lactic acid. The sickness, muscle weakness, and sweating you experience after you’ve pushed it too hard at the gym is the feeling of anaerobic overload. This process explains why the first few minutes of an intense workout is often so miserable. Our lungs and respiratory system haven’t caught up to supply the oxygen our bodies need, and so the body has to use anaerobic respiration. This also explains why, after we’re warmed up, exercise feels easier. The body has switched from anaerobic to aerobic respiration.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글 전체는 유산소·무산소 호흡이 어떻게 운동 수행에 에너지를 공급하는지를 설명한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① the best diet to eat before intense exercise(격렬한 운동 전 최적의 식단): 식단은 다루지 않았어요.

❌ ② the permanent muscle damage caused by lactic acid(젖산이 일으키는 영구적 근육 손상): 세부 언급일 뿐 주제가 아니에요.

✅ ③ how aerobic and anaerobic energy fuel exercise(유산소·무산소 에너지가 운동에 연료를 공급하는 방식): 글 전체를 아우르는 주제예요 ←정답

❌ ④ the long history of studies on human breathing(인체 호흡 연구의 오랜 역사): 연구의 역사는 나오지 않아요.
det.tip: breathing + aerobic/anaerobic + performance = 글의 핵심
